planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade.

directions: Brigadoon is a vigorous Camellia x williamsii hybrid holding the RHS Award of Garden Merit, producing large, pink, semi-double to peony-form flowers over a long late-winter-into-spring season. Like other members of the williamsii grex first raised from a cross of C. japonica and C. saluenensis at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall, it sheds spent blooms cleanly and tolerates more open sun than straight japonica cultivars. Plant in acidic, humus-rich soil with dappled shade from hot afternoon sun, and mulch to keep roots cool and evenly moist through summer. Its dense, bushy habit takes well to light post-bloom pruning for hedging or screening use.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade.

directions: Glenn's Orbit is a Camellia x williamsii hybrid grown for its anemone-to-peony-form deep pink flowers. As with other williamsii hybrids descended from the original C. japonica x C. saluenensis cross made at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall, it blooms earlier and tolerates more sun than straight japonica camellias. Site it in acidic, well-drained soil with afternoon shade in hotter climates, and water deeply while buds form in late summer. Its habit is dense and upright, taking well to light formative pruning right after bloom.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade.

directions: Ruby Wedding is a Camellia x williamsii hybrid holding the RHS Award of Garden Merit, bearing deep red flowers that fit the anniversary theme many camellia introductions use for their names. It shares the williamsii grex's general ease of culture, inherited from the C. japonica x C. saluenensis cross first made at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall, including a longer bloom season and better sun tolerance than most japonica cultivars. Grow in humus-rich, acidic soil with consistent moisture, and avoid exposed sites where hard frost can damage open flowers. Deadhead spent blooms where reachable to keep the dense, upright plant tidy through its long flowering period.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade.

directions: E.T.R. Carlyon is a Camellia x williamsii hybrid honored with the RHS Award of Garden Merit, producing large white flowers blushed with pink, semi-double, on a vigorous, upright bush. Like other members of the williamsii grex descended from the original C. japonica x C. saluenensis cross at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall, it flowers earlier in the season and tolerates more open sun than most japonica cultivars. Plant in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil and provide steady moisture while flower buds swell in late summer and fall. Prune lightly right after bloom to maintain shape, since next year's buds set on the current season's growth.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade.

directions: Clarrie Fawcett is a Camellia x williamsii hybrid recognized with the RHS Award of Garden Merit, bearing pale pink, semi-double flowers over a long winter-to-spring season. It inherits the williamsii grex's relative sun tolerance and early flowering from the C. japonica x C. saluenensis parentage first combined at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall. Grow in acidic, humus-rich soil with reliable moisture, siting it where afternoon shade protects flowers from scorching in hotter inland gardens. Its naturally rounded, dense habit needs little formative pruning beyond removing dead or crossing wood after bloom.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade.

directions: Bowen Bryant is a pink-flowered Camellia x williamsii hybrid valued among collectors for the reliable, early flowering and easy-care nature typical of the williamsii grex. That grex traces to the original cross of C. japonica and C. saluenensis made at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall in the early twentieth century, which combined japonica's hardiness with saluenensis's sun tolerance and earlier bloom. Grow it in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade in warmer climates, and keep the root zone consistently moist through the summer bud-set period. Light pruning right after flowering keeps the naturally dense habit shapely without sacrificing next year's bloom.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade.

directions: Daintiness is an RHS Award of Garden Merit-winning Camellia x williamsii hybrid with salmon-pink flowers, grown for the floriferous, long winter-to-spring bloom season typical of its grex. Williamsii hybrids like this one descend from the original C. japonica x C. saluenensis cross made at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall, which gave the group earlier flowering and better tolerance of open sun than straight japonica cultivars. Site it in acidic, humus-rich soil with steady moisture, sheltering it from the hardest winter frosts while buds are open. Its compact, dense habit suits foundation plantings or large containers better than more sprawling williamsii selections.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade.

directions: Julia Hamiter is a pink and white Camellia x williamsii hybrid recognized with the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its dependable, abundant flowering. Like other williamsii hybrids, it descends from the cross of C. japonica and C. saluenensis first made at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall, a pairing that produced plants tolerating more sun and flowering earlier than japonica alone. Plant in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil, and water deeply during dry stretches in late summer when next season's flower buds are forming. Prune only lightly, right after bloom, to preserve the naturally full, rounded shape.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade.

directions: Señorita is a pink-flowered Camellia x williamsii hybrid carrying the RHS Award of Garden Merit, prized for the long, reliable bloom season characteristic of the williamsii grex. The grex originated from a cross between C. japonica and C. saluenensis first made at Caerhays Castle in Cornwall, combining japonica's cold hardiness with saluenensis's earlier flowering and tolerance for more open sun. Grow it in humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil, mulching to keep roots cool through summer heat. Light shaping after flowering is usually all the pruning it needs to stay dense and floriferous.
